results.title: B200 GPU price per hour: 6 clouds ranked, Sep 2026
highlights:
- Ranked by the lowest listed on-demand B200 price per GPU-hour, checked 28 September 2026, Modal ($6.25), Lambda ($6.69) and RunPod ($6.79) sit within 54 cents of each other. 1 3 4
- Modal’s rate buys the GPU alone. CPU and memory are billed on top, so its lead narrows or disappears once a host is attached. 1
- Crusoe and DigitalOcean list no on-demand B200 price. Crusoe sends B200 instance buyers to sales; DigitalOcean’s GPU Droplet list has no B200 at all. 5 6
- A B200 hour costs 1.40 to 2.05 times an H100 hour at the same provider. It carries 180 GB of memory against 80 GB, so it’s cheaper per gigabyte of GPU memory everywhere we could compare. 3 4 2
- Interruptible capacity roughly halves the price: Together AI lists preemptible B200s at $4.09 and CoreWeave’s spot node works out to $4.26 per GPU. 7 2
- Nebius lists $8.50 from 1 October 2026, up from $7.15, which drops it from fourth to fifth. 8
- The hourly rate is only one input to what a model costs to run. Our explainer on what controls AI inference cost covers the rest of the bill.

...

- Source: each provider’s public pricing page, captured 28 September 2026.
- Field: the lowest listed on-demand B200 price per GPU-hour at each provider. HGX B200 and B200 SXM6 listings both count.
- Unit: US dollars per GPU per hour, before tax. Lambda lists its prices “plus applicable sales tax/VAT/GST”. 3 Nebius shows all prices “without any applicable taxes, including VAT”. 8
- Conversions: CoreWeave prices a whole 8-GPU node, so its node price is divided by eight. Modal prices per second, so its rate is multiplied by 3,600. No other figure is changed.
- Row count: nine pages captured, eight providers checked, six listing an on-demand B200 price, six ranked.
- Not ranked: Crusoe and DigitalOcean, which list no on-demand B200 price; Vast.ai, whose prices are set by hosts on a marketplace; spot, preemptible and reserved rates, which have their own section below.

...

Crusoe is the clearest case among the eight. Its GPU instance table lists the 180 GB HGX B200 with “Contact sales” in both the on-demand and spot columns, while it prints $3.90 per GPU-hour for the H100. 5 The only B200 figure Crusoe publishes is $9.65 an hour for a self-serve managed inference deployment, which is a dedicated model endpoint, not an instance rental. 5

DigitalOcean doesn’t list the B200 at all. Its GPU Droplet page, repriced from 1 August 2026, lists B300, H200, H100, L40S, RTX Ada and AMD Instinct GPUs, with no B200 in the on-demand, spot or reserved plans. 6

...

At the same provider, a B200 hour costs between 1.40 and 2.05 times an H100 hour, checked 28 September 2026. The gap in dollars runs from $2.30 at Modal to $4.20 at Together AI. Each pair below compares the provider’s B200 with its own SXM-class or HGX H100 on the same terms.

...

## What changes in October 2026?

Nebius has published its next B200 rate: $8.50 per GPU-hour from 1 October 2026, up $1.35, or 19%, from $7.15. 8 At $8.50 it moves from fourth to fifth, behind Together AI’s $8.19 and just ahead of CoreWeave’s $8.60. Its H100 rises at the same time, from $3.85 to $4.50, so its B200-to-H100 ratio barely moves, from 1.86 to 1.89. 8

Other pages were repriced recently. RunPod dates its pricing page 27 September 2026, and DigitalOcean’s new GPU pricing took effect on 1 August 2026. 4 6 Together AI’s page carries a banner saying on-demand B200s are now available on its GPU Clusters. 7 This research snapshot includes no earlier B200 price ranking to compare.

## How does each provider bill for GPU time?

Six of the eight state a price per GPU-hour, Modal states a price per second and CoreWeave states a price per 8-GPU node-hour. The metering behind the headline differs again.

results.title: Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay
results.author: Bobby Clay
highlights:
# Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in … | Bobby Clay · LinkedIn · 2026-10-05T00:00:00+00:00

**Bobby Clay**.

---

Nebius did exactly what it said it would. Last week's Pulse flagged the on-demand increases Nebius had posted for October 1. Our October 4 catalog capture yesterday shows them in place, in dollars per GPU-hour:

H100: $3.85 to $4.50
H200: $4.50 to $5.40
B200: $7.15 to $8.50
B300: $7.85 to $9.50

That changed the lowest observed H100 list price across the nine providers we track. On September 27 it was Nebius at $3.85 per GPU-hour. On October 4 it was Crusoe at $3.90.
Everything else held. Of 14,001 GPU price listings in the October 4 catalog, 13,996 matched a September 27 listing, and the 20 Nebius listings were the only verified changes above 1%.

The transaction side moved on its own path. OCPI for H200 went from $4.84 on September 28 to $5.57 on October 4. Over the same stretch, the lowest H200 list price we track held at $4.29 (Crusoe). List prices and transaction prices measure different things, and this week the gap between them widened. If you buy on-demand capacity from a Neocloud, posted price notices are worth tracking. This one landed on schedule, to the cent.

The full issue, with every provider's lowest observed price and the method notes, is here:
https://lnkd.in/efqfwQWm

These are public catalog list prices, not live quotes, and a listing does not establish capacity or orderability.

results.title: Nebius GPU prices rise across the board, up to… · Slicast
highlights:
Trade press Slicast · October 1, 2026 at 21:01 UTC · Global · Source: KuCoin News

A notable shift is emerging in the AI computing power market: while cloud providers continue to expand their data centers, rental prices for certain high-end GPUs are not declining with increased supply—they continue to rise.

According to a price adjustment notice sent by Nebius to its customers, effective October 1, 2026, the company plans to increase prices for multiple on-demand GPU instances by approximately 17% to 21%. The proposed hourly rates per GPU are: H100 rising from $3.85 to $4.50 (a 16.9% increase), H200 from $4.50 to $5.40 (20% increase), B200 from $7.15 to $8.50 (18.9% increase), and B300 from $7.85 to $9.50 (21% increase).

This price adjustment sends a significant signal: the pace of growth in AI computing demand may still outstrip the rate at which high-end GPUs, power, and data center capacity are coming online. Unlike traditional cloud computing, the core scarce resources for AI cloud services extend beyond servers to include GPU availability, power access, liquid cooling systems, networking equipment, and data centers capable of supporting high-density racks. If any single component encounters a bottleneck, new computing power cannot be rapidly deployed.

At the Goldman Sachs Technology Conference, Nebius management stated that the company's visibility into customer demand has extended from approximately 18 months to over 24 months, with some customers already reserving compute capacity for the first half of 2028. The company previously conducted price testing for scarce Blackwell

...

The significance of Nebius's price increase lies not merely in the ability to charge approximately 20% more per GPU hour, but in confirming that supply and demand in the AI computing market still favor suppliers. A primary past market concern was that simultaneous launches of numerous data centers could eventually lead to GPU leasing market oversupply, potentially resulting in lower utilization rates, extended payback periods, and asset impairment for companies built under assumptions of higher prices. Nebius signals the opposite: the company is raising prices not only for new B200 and B300 models but also for H100 and H200, which have been on the market for years. This indicates that demand extends beyond the latest architecture, with previous-generation GPUs still offering sufficient performance and cost efficiency for model fine-tuning, inference, scientific computing, and certain enterprise workloads.

...

However, the on-demand price increase will not uniformly raise all of Nebius's revenue by 20%. Large customers typically sign multi-year contracts with fixed prices, minimum purchase volumes, and service terms that cannot be immediately repriced according to new public rates. This adjustment most directly impacts on-demand and short-term compute contracts rather than long-term capacity agreements already signed by clients like Meta.

results.title: DigitalOcean is introducing an all-inclusive… · Slicast
highlights:
Trade press Slicast · October 1, 2026 at 12:15 UTC · US · Source: Diginomica

D igitalOcean has reshaped itself from the cloud that made $5 servers simple into what it now calls the AI-Native Cloud. Today it launches Agent Droplets, a subscription that bundles compute, memory, storage, inference, and tool access into a single monthly price—$50 for a solo developer, $200 for a team—with discounts of 15% and 20% respectively across everything an agent consumes.

...

The press release explicitly mentions five-hour and weekly usage windows and per-seat charges—pricing structures used by Cursor and Claude Code—as models Agent Droplets are designed to differ from. Srinivasan observed that developers were managing their billing plan instead of their work, whereas Agent Droplets are built around actual usage so the main constraint is the work itself rather than an arbitrary window or headcount. For context, GitHub Copilot moved to metered AI credits in June 2026, Cursor operates a credit-pool-plus-overage model, and Claude Code caps usage on rolling five-hour windows. Pricing across AI coding tools has fragmented significantly over the past year.

results.title: GPU Prices 2026: H100 From $3.49/hr, RTX 5070 at +58%
results.author: Axis Intelligence Research
highlights:
> Prices verified on October 2, 2026. Every price on this page was read from the vendor’s live pricing page, public price API or retail listing on that date. AWS Capacity Block rates effective October 7, 2026 are taken from AWS’s own announcement on its pricing page.

...

How much does a GPU cost in October 2026? In the cloud, an NVIDIA H100 lists between $3.49 and $12.29 per GPU-hour on-demand; the neocloud median is $3.99. A B200 lists from $6.69 to $8.60. On the consumer side, the cheapest new RTX 5070 on Newegg was $869.99 against a $549 launch price — 58% above MSRP.

...

1. According to Axis Intelligence Research, hyperscalers list the NVIDIA H100 at 2.93 times the neocloud median price — $11.68 versus $3.99 per GPU-hour on-demand, as of October 2, 2026 (GPU Hour Premium Ratio, GHPR).
2. AWS raises EC2 Capacity Block GPU rates about 15% effective October 7, 2026, taking an H100 accelerator-hour from $5.191 to $5.970 and a B200 from $12.355 to $14.208, per AWS’s pricing page.
3. An 8-GPU H100 server rented on-demand for three years costs $2.58 million on Azure and $734,000 on Runpod, according to Axis Intelligence Research’s list-price TCO calculation.
4. The cheapest new GeForce RTX 5070 on Newegg cost $869.99 on October 2, 2026, 58% above the $549 price NVIDIA announced at CES in January 2025.
5. Azure’s spot price for an 8x H100 VM is 82% below its own on-demand rate — $18.17 versus $98.32 per hour in US East, per Microsoft’s Retail Prices API.

...

AWS’s per-accelerator figure that we verified is the EC2 Capacity Blocks for ML rate — a reservation you book for a fixed window, not open-ended on-demand. On October 2, 2026 the p5.48xlarge (8x H100) Capacity Block rate in US East (N. Virginia) was $41.528 per instance-hour, or $5.191 per H100. AWS’s pricing page states that from October 7, 2026, the P5 rate becomes $5.970 per accelerator across all available regions. Axis Intelligence Research did not verify a current AWS on-demand p5 rate for this snapshot, so AWS is excluded from the on-demand table rather than estimated.

...

results.title: Recompute Token Cost Before Q4 GPU Reservations — The Serving Desk
results.author: 3 MIN
highlights:
GPU reservations trade committed capacity for a fixed rate, but a fixed rate can become a stale rate when on-demand prices move. The arithmetic is simple: cost per token equals the GPU-hour rate divided by tokens per GPU-hour, so the percentage change in rate becomes the percentage change in token cost when throughput holds. Nebius, an AI cloud provider, is repricing its Nvidia GPU fleet on October 1, the second on-demand reset in three months.

The H100 moves from $3.85 to $4.50 per GPU-hour, a 16.9% increase. H200 and B200 rates move to $5.40 and $8.50 per GPU-hour, increases of 20% and 18.9%. The B300 jumps from $7.85 to $9.50 on October 1, a 21% increase.

### 6. Paperspace by DigitalOcean Review (2026)

 VPSRated Rating: 9.2 / 10 — Best for Jupyter Notebooks & Prototyping 

 Overview: Now backed by the enterprise infrastructure of DigitalOcean, Paperspace specializes in eliminating DevOps friction for data scientists. Its core product, Gradient, provides a fully managed Jupyter notebook workspace backed by dedicated GPU compute, automated versioning, and zero-configuration environment setup.

- Billing Model: Hourly billing combined with monthly tier subscriptions.
- Persistent Storage: High-speed shared workspace storage with automated snapshots and Git integration.
- Networking: Standard 1 Gbps to 10 Gbps networking integrated into DigitalOcean's global private VPC backbone.
- Global Regions: US East (NY2), US West (CA1), and Europe (Amsterdam AMS1).
- Developer Experience: Easiest platform for non-DevOps practitioners. Launch an interactive PyTorch or Hugging Face notebook in one click.

- Zero setup overhead: interactive Jupyter notebooks ready in seconds.
- Free GPU quota included in monthly Pro/Growth subscriptions.
- Seamless integration with DigitalOcean Droplets and databases.

- Fewer cutting-edge GPUs (no B200 HGX or H200 yet).
